historicalLabelIgnored: Per constraint 5 this is severity-assessed AT HEAD TODAY. Its historical `high` label carries NO weight in this classification.
impact: The nudge pot (protocol incentive funds) is claimable by a caller whose payment bears no relation to what they take. The qualification gate at :351-352 is `qualifies = _nudgeSize != 0 && count >= _nudgeSize` — literally a COUNT compared to a COUNT — so a 1× payer and a 1000× payer receive byte-identical payouts. Measured: attacker pays 5,256.33 pay-token for count=5 and takes the 50,000 pot; an honest count=50 batch pays 110,294.59 and receives 0. Three refill cycles captured 150,000. Cost-to-qualify vs pot ≈ 9.5× net-positive; NudgeDrain Variant B cost 5e6 vs pot 100,000e6 → 20,000×.
attackPath: 1. The pot accumulates from an unbounded, time-accumulating stream: StableYieldAccumulator.claim() routes nudgeSplit% to the nudge address (StableYieldAccumulator.sol:512-516), with no relationship to mint cost.
2. Top-up is PERMISSIONLESS — BatchNFTMinter.sol:45-46: 'Anyone can seed the batch incentive with any ERC20 simply by sending it here. No owner transaction is involved.'
3. A searcher waits for the pot to exceed nudgeSize × mintPrice (a lull in batching, bots offline, gas spike, UI outage — nothing in code brakes it).
4. The searcher submits the minimum qualifying batch and takes the entire balance-based payout.
5. The honest large batcher who actually generated the demand receives 0.
likelihood: medium — the mechanic is executed and permissionless, but the profitability precondition (pot ≥ nudgeSize × mintPrice) is NOT satisfied on mainnet today (observed margin ~6×, the safe direction). Nothing in the contract enforces the margin; only bot competition does.
assumptions: The pot grows past the cost of the qualifying batch. Empirically not true today; structurally unbounded.
externalRequirements: A funding lull or an unusually large SYA drip, plus a searcher watching. Present on-chain exposure is ZERO (D-22).
justification: C4 Medium at HEAD: a value leak reachable by a hypothetical-but-executed attack path, with stated assumptions and external requirements. NOT High — the profitability precondition is not currently met on mainnet, RatchetBatchNFTMinter holds 0 of everything, archive reads confirm 0 at the block before the fix so no historical loss occurred, and no principal theft appears in ANY of the 11 replay tests. NOT Low — the mechanic is proven live by execution at HEAD, top-up is permissionless so nothing owner-side bounds it, and the design document's own safety claim is backed by no code.

whatExpired.leg2_overFundedPotIsOwnerDriven: ✗ DEAD. The closure read 'residual value-blindness only exploitable via owner misconfiguration ⇒ owner-driven ⇒ invalid'. At HEAD, over-funding is NOT an owner action at all. Law 3 protects the owner-trusted surface; it cannot reach a facet a permissionless third-party stream and any unrelated address can reach without the owner. The '⇒ owner-driven, invalid' inference fails ON ITS OWN PREMISE. This is not a re-litigation of Law 3 — it is the observation that the predicate Law 3 was applied to is false at HEAD.
